title: a buffer pin: an open cursor keeps a page pinned, and VACUUM has to work around it

steps.note: T1 opens a cursor over accounts and fetches one row. the scan stops there, holding a pin on page 0 until the cursor moves on or closes.

steps.sql:
SELECT relblocknumber AS block, pinning_backends
FROM pg_buffercache
WHERE relfilenode = pg_relation_filenode('accounts')
  AND relforknumber = 0
  AND reldatabase = (SELECT oid FROM pg_database WHERE datname = current_database())
ORDER BY relblocknumber
steps.note: pg_buffercache counts the pin: one backend is pinning the table's page 0.

steps.sql: UPDATE accounts SET balance = 110.00 WHERE id = 1
steps.note: a pin doesn't stop writers. T2 updates alice on the pinned page: it only needs the page's content lock, for a moment.
VACUUM needs more than a content lock to remove dead tuples: a cleanup lock, which means nobody else has the page pinned. it can't get one, so it leaves the dead version of bob where it is.
